:::{#exm-matrix-induced-inner-product}
#### A matrix-induced inner product calculation

Consider the symmetric matrix

$$
\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}.
$$

For any nonzero vector $\vx = (x_1, x_2) \in \reals^2$:

$$
\ba
\tp{\vx}\matr{A}\vx
&= 2 x_1^2 + 2 x_1 x_2 + 2 x_2^2
&& \text{(expand the quadratic form)}
\\
&= (x_1 + x_2)^2 + x_1^2 + x_2^2
&& \text{(complete the square)}
\ea
$$

which is strictly positive because $x_1^2 + x_2^2 > 0$ when $\vx \neq \vzero$.
Thus $\matr{A}$ is positive definite (@def-positive-definite).

For vectors $\vx = (1, 2)$ and $\vy = (3, -1)$,
their inner product induced by $\matr{A}$ is:

$$
\ba
\iprod{\vx}{\vy}_{\matr{A}}
&= \tp{\vx} \matr{A} \vy
&& \text{(definition of } \iprod{\cdot}{\cdot}_{\matr{A}} \text{)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(substitute vectors and matrix)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 2 \cd 3 + 1 \cd (-1) \\ 1 \cd 3 + 2 \cd (-1) \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(@def-matvec-mult)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(multiply and add)}
\\
&= 1 \cd 5 + 2 \cd 1
&& \text{(@def-matvec-mult)}
\\
&= 7.
&& \text{(multiply and add)}
\ea
$$

In contrast, the standard dot product yields:

$$
\vx \cdot \vy = 1 \cd 3 + 2 \cd (-1) = 1.
$$

The off-diagonal entries $A_{12} = A_{21} = 1$ couple the coordinate directions,
altering lengths and angles from their Euclidean values.
When $\matr{A} = \matr{I}_p$, the matrix-induced inner product recovers the standard dot product $\iprod{\vx}{\vy}_{\matr{I}_p} = \vx \cdot \vy$.

:::
